Engaged and answered in two parts; the second part is why this row is threatened rather than clean. PART ONE, the reachability question: gating the job to pull_request opens no new path to main. A PR merged to main fires pull_request first, where the job runs and completeness IS enforced. A direct push to main was ALREADY completeness-free before this change, which I proved by execution rather than by reading: I checked out origin/main in a throwaway detached worktree and ran the checker against it in push mode, and it exited 0 reporting `completeness: scoped to 0 entries changed since origin/main` (merge-base equals HEAD there, so the touched-entry set at :265 is empty and :135 leaves `missing` empty for every entry). What the push path DOES lose is per-entry shape validation, which previously ran on every push; the always-run `node scripts/invariant-shape-check.mjs` step that would restore it is deliberately deferred, because that script does not exist here or on origin/main (`git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main | grep -c invariant-shape-check` returned 0; it appears only on the unmerged commit 14ffb32, which `git branch -a --contains` places solely on feat/invariant-inert-registry), so adding the step would red every run. PART TWO, the census question, which is the threat: the new test classifies workflow steps and run-line tokens, so it is itself a gate M2 governs. Its site census is closed and halts correctly — `assert.equal(sites.length, 1, ...)` at ci-invariant-wiring.test.mjs:136 refuses to proceed when the number of checker invocation sites is not exactly one, which makes the guard assertions exhaustive rather than sampled, and I confirmed by grep that .github/workflows/test.yml is the only workflow referencing the checker. But SCOPE_FLAGS at :10 is a hand-maintained `['--event', '--base-ref']`, a restatement of a subset of the checker's own FLAGS at scripts/invariant-coverage-check.mjs:13 (`['--root', '--event', '--base-ref']`) rather than a derivation from it. Today the sample happens to be complete, since --root is not a CI scope input (the checker defaults it at :252) — but nothing halts if the checker grows a fourth scope-bearing input, so the test would silently keep checking two flags. That is the sampled allowlist M2 forbids. Mitigation, not yet applied: derive the checked flag set from the checker's exported FLAGS so an unclassified scope input halts. Named here rather than fixed, because closing it means changing the checker's export surface, which is outside this unit.
